title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi celebrates Diwali with the security forces at CoBRA Operations Base at Karanpur in Bastar, Chhattisgarh
subtitle:
This is the first Diwali when every district in country is free from Naxalism: PM

For the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF jawan had to lose their life during duty in the past one year; This is a triumph of the nation's sound policies and strong resolve: PM

Driven by a spirit of service, we have transformed lives in Naxal-affected areas; as a result, even the victims of Naxalism have stood firmly alongside the government and security forces: PM

Today, on one hand, 50 crore people have come out of extreme poverty; On the other hand, Naxal violence has also come to an end in the country: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 NOV 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today visited the CoBRA Operations Base at Karanpur in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, which served as the training base and launch pad for counter-Naxal operations in Bastar and Abujhmad, to celebrate Diwali with the security forces. Addressing the jawans on the occasion as crores of Indians across the nation and the world celebrate the sacred festival of lights with their loved ones, the Prime Minister recalled his memorable Diwali celebrations with brave soldiers from Kargil and Lepcha in the Himalayas to Sir Creek on the coast and aboard INS Vikrant in the ocean. “At the borders and within the country, the sentinels of the nation who protect the country, the brave sons of Maa Bharati, all of you are my loved ones, all of you are a part of my family,” remarked Shri Modi.
Describing the 2026 Diwali as truly special because it marks the first festival of lights after India won its decades-old battle against Maoist terror, rendered every district Naxal-free, and enabled crores of citizens to overcome fear, the Prime Minister explained that he had come to Bastar to celebrate this extraordinary milestone with the lakhs of security personnel who made it possible and to convey the gratitude of 140 crore citizens. “Today I have come to express gratitude towards your sacrifice, dedication, and spirit of service,” affirmed PM Modi.
Quoting the ancient Sanskrit wisdom ‘Aabhyantaram Bhayam Rakshyam, Asaaram Baahyato Bhayam’ to explain that external enemies cannot harm a nation whose internal security is strong but raise their heads when internal security weakens, the Prime Minister equated the internal role of security forces with that of the armed forces at the borders and lauded the boundless sacrifices of personnel from the CRPF, CoBRA, BSF, ITBP, SSB, IRB, state police forces, Bastar Fighters commandos, and women fighters, while also extending festive greetings to soldiers guarding the nation's frontiers. “This country is indebted to you for your services, and crores of countrymen are proud of you,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Recalling the grim era when Left-Wing Extremism gripped over 230 districts across nearly 20 states including Bihar, Maharashtra, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh, where evening curfews of fear prevailed, voting rights were snatched, up to 2,000 annual attacks occurred, over 1,000 personnel laid down their lives in Chhattisgarh alone, countless soldiers lost limbs to IED blasts, and 76 CRPF personnel and 44 innocent civilians were killed in separate 2010 Dantewada attacks, the Prime Minister pointed out that between 2004 and 2013 more security personnel were martyred annually than Naxals killed, emboldening Maoist leaders.
Emphasizing that no nation can progress with a passive approach toward its enemies and must instead crush them strategically with high morale, the Prime Minister stated that after 2014, reversing the decades-old trend of higher casualties among security forces and resulting in a historic milestone where not a single CRPF soldier lost their life on duty over the past year for the first time in 47 years. “This is the victory of the country's right policies and firm willpower, and this is the victory of your valor, courage, and restraint,” asserted Shri Modi.
Stating that success requires both the right intention and the right policies, the Prime Minister noted that the government took a series of tough, including several unpublicized, national security decisions that struck at Naxal and separatist funding and destroyed the fake currency nexus. “Not only did this break their economic backbone, rather the entire supply line was choked, stopping the supply of weapons and curbing the movement and recruitment of Naxals,” noted PM Modi.
The Prime Minister stated that his government granted full operational freedom to security forces to take every necessary decision. Explaining that the government worked tirelessly without publicity or ostentation toward the singular goal of ensuring no mother loses her child, no family is ruined, and no youth takes up arms, he highlighted how combining sensitive security operations that broke the back of Maoist terror with a spirit of public service transformed lives and rallied affected citizens behind the government and security forces, including local citizens present at the event whom he thanked for their vital cooperation. “With a spirit of service, we transformed the lives of people in Naxal-affected areas,” remarked PM Modi.
Observing that working with the spirit of Nation First ensures peace and security, propels the country to new developmental heights, and expands the participation of the poor and deprived in national progress, the Prime Minister pointed out the dual triumph achieved by the nation over the past dozen years. “In the past 12 years, the country has not only won the battle against Naxalism and separatism, rather the country has also won a major war against poverty,” asserted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the widely discussed World Bank report released just ahead of Deepavali, the Prime Minister noted that 50 crore Indians have escaped extreme poverty over the past 12 years.
Comparing India's welfare architecture over the past 12 years to a Diwali Rangoli where small, distinct lines come together to form a grand picture, the Prime Minister detailed how Jan Dhan banking, PM Awas pucca homes, collateral-free Mudra loans, SVANidhi support for street vendors, Ayushman Bharat healthcare, free monthly rations, child education policies, Swachh Bharat, and Har Ghar Jal collectively ensured free medicine, free education, and a free kitchen while removing basic anxieties so families once trapped in generational poverty now inherit a stronger future. “The poor families whose entire lives used to be spent only in worry have now received the assurance of the government, and a new self-confidence has come into them,” noted Shri Modi.
Pointing out that this victory over poverty is deeply linked to the fight against Naxalism, which previously trapped lakhs of innocent citizens in deprivation by blocking schools, hospitals, medical stores, polio vaccinations, mobile towers, and industries while bombing railway tracks, the Prime Minister detailed the special development drive in Left-Wing Extremism-affected areas that built over 15,000 kilometers of roads, over 9,500 mobile towers, nearly 175 Eklavya schools, around 50 ITIs, 50 Skill Development Centres, and thousands of post offices, bank branches, and ATMs, alongside rehabilitating surrendered Naxals and bringing water, electricity, and roads to remote tribal villages for the first time under PM JANMAN. “When we started the fight against Naxalism, at the same time we also ran special campaigns for the development of Naxal-affected areas,” noted PM Modi.
Stating that the ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’ campaign energized the fight against poverty and brought an end to Naxal violence alongside lifting 50 crore people out of extreme poverty, the Prime Minister cited the ongoing Bastar Olympics as a symbol of transformation in the region. “Today in this very Bastar, the Bastar Olympics are taking place, and children are trying their hand at sports, not guns,” remarked Shri Modi.
Emphasizing that today's milestones are a launchpad rather than a stopping point, the Prime Minister stated that the nation's new flight will fulfill the centuries-old dreams of freedom fighters, border soldiers, and personnel who laid down their lives fighting Naxalism and terrorism, urging the forces who live by the motto ‘Tera Gaurav Amar Rahe Maa, Hum Din Chaar Rahein Na Rahein’ to channel their spirit into new confidence. “Now is the time to live for the nation and to take the nation to a new height,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Citing the nation's proven track record of fulfilling major pledges such as abrogating Article 370 in Kashmir, building household toilets, and expanding vaccination coverage, the Prime Minister expressed complete confidence in the security forces and citizens that India will similarly achieve its goals of eradicating poverty and building a Drug-Free, Atmanirbhar, and Viksit Bharat, urging everyone to work toward witnessing these dreams become a reality before concluding with Deepavali greetings. “Your sacrifices and hard work will become a strong foundation for the grand edifice of a Viksit Bharat,” affirmed PM Modi.

title: English rendering of PM's speech during interaction with the Security Forces in Bastar, Chhattisgarh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 NOV 2026 2:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Bharat Mata Ki Jai.
Bharat Mata Ki Jai.
Bharat Mata Ki Jai.
My dear countrymen,
Today, crores of Indians across the country and in every corner of the world are celebrating the sacred festival of lights. People are travelling from far and wide to reach their homes. It is a great festival of meeting and spending time with family and loved ones. And I too have come among you to celebrate Diwali. Whether on the borders or within the country, all of you who defend the nation, all of you who stand guard over the nation, all you brave sons and daughters of Mother India, are my own people, a part of my family. From Kargil in the lap of the Himalayas to Lepcha, from Sir Creek on the seashore to INS Vikrant in the embrace of the sea, every Diwali spent with our brave soldiers has been memorable for me.
My brave soldiers,
This time, I have come to celebrate Diwali in the forests of Bastar, among all of you. This is the land where Naxalite terror once held sway, and because of your sacrifice, dedication, and perseverance, that very land has now been freed from the scourge of Naxalite terror and has begun a new journey of development.
And friends,
This Diwali of 2026 is truly special. After forty or fifty years, such a Diwali has arrived for all of you. This is the first Diwali when the country has won its decades-long battle against Naxalism and Maoist terror. This is the first Diwali when every district of the country is free from Naxalism. This is the first Diwali when crores of citizens have overcome the fear of Naxalism. This is an extraordinary achievement. A very large share of the credit belongs to you, to lakhs of brave personnel like you, to our soldiers, sons and daughters, and security personnel. Therefore, today I have come to celebrate Diwali with you. And I have also come to express, on behalf of 140 crore Indians, gratitude for your sacrifice, dedication, and spirit of service.
Friends,
Our visionary ancestors said: “Abhyantaram bhayam rakshyam, asaram bahyato bhayam.” This means that when a nation’s internal security is strong, external enemies cannot do much harm. But when internal security weakens, external enemies also begin to raise their heads. Therefore, the role that our armed forces play on the borders is the same role that all of you security personnel play within the country. You have made countless sacrifices for the unity and integrity of the nation. You have shown limitless dedication. The security forces engaged in preserving internal security, our CRPF, CoBRA, BSF, ITBP, every single jawan, the SSB, IRB, the police personnel of the states, the commandos of special forces such as the Bastar Fighters, and our women fighters, this nation is indebted to all of you for your service. Crores and crores of citizens are proud of you. With this feeling of gratitude and affection, I extend my heartfelt Diwali greetings to every one of you, wherever you are standing guard. I also convey my greetings to our soldiers deployed on the borders for the defence of the nation.
Friends,
This battle against Maoist terror and Naxalism was not easy. There was a time when more than 230 districts across nearly 20 states of the country were affected by Naxalism. After sunset, life would come to a standstill in these areas. It became impossible to step outside one's home. These Naxalites had even snatched away the people's right to vote. Bihar, Maharashtra, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh, a very large part of the country was affected by Left-wing extremism. Thousands of villages and crores of people were trapped by it. There were as many as two thousand Naxalite attacks in a single year. Just remember, in 2010, nearby in Dantewada, 76 CRPF personnel were martyred in an encounter with Naxalites. In the same year, another incident in Dantewada claimed the lives of 44 innocent civilians. This land was consecrated by the blood of our brave men. But not a single cry of grief was heard from those privileged leaders living in their palaces. Not even a single tear emerged from their eyes. Such attacks occurred repeatedly. This cycle continued for decades. During this period, more than one thousand security personnel sacrificed their lives in Chhattisgarh alone. Many soldiers lost their arms and legs in IED blasts. If you look at the figures from 2004 to 2013, every year more of our brave soldiers were martyred than the number of Naxalites eliminated. The leaders of Naxalite organisations considered this their victory and celebrated it. And unfortunately, the governments of that time had accepted Naxalism as an incurable disease and simply left it unattended. My tribal families were left to survive on their fate. It had been accepted that this would continue endlessly, bullets would keep flying, soldiers would keep dying, and innocent citizens would keep suffering.
Friends,
No nation can function with an attitude of “this is how things will continue.” To move a nation forward, its enemies must be crushed with determination, courage, and a clear strategy. The political will that was lacking in the country for this task was restored in 2014. You gave this Pradhan Sevak an opportunity to serve Mother India. And after 2014, we saw both the situation and the statistics begin to change. For years, discussions revolved around the number of security personnel being killed compared to the number of Naxalites. But after 47 years, for the first time, not a single CRPF jawan lost his life during duty over the past year. This is the victory of the country's correct policies and firm resolve. This is the victory of your bravery, your courage, and your restraint. I repeat, this is the victory of your bravery, your courage, and your restraint.
Bharat Mata Ki Jai.
Bharat Mata Ki Jai.
Victory to these brave soldiers.
Our security forces and police personnel remained steadfast even in the most adverse circumstances. This is the victory of that devotion to duty.
Friends,
Success requires the right intentions and the right policies. For national security, we took one tough decision after another. Many such steps were also taken that are still not known to the public. Through these decisions and efforts, a major blow was dealt to the funding networks of Naxalites and separatists. The nexus of fake currency was destroyed. This not only broke their financial backbone but also choked their entire supply chain. As a result, the supply of weapons stopped, and restrictions were imposed on the movement and recruitment of Naxalites.
Friends,
Previous governments had also tied the hands of the security forces fighting on the ground. Naxalite attacks kept taking place, but the security forces did not have the freedom to retaliate decisively. We gave the security forces the freedom to take every necessary decision. We also worked to stop the support that Left-wing extremism used to receive from certain people sitting within the government and the system.
Friends,
We were pursuing a very large goal. Our goal was that no mother's lap should be left empty, no family should be trapped in a cycle of destruction, no child should pick up weapons and walk the path of violence, and no young person's future should be ruined. Therefore, until this goal was achieved, we continued to work with determination. There was no publicity, no display. Working with sensitivity, we broke the backbone of Maoist terror. Through a spirit of service, we transformed lives in Naxal-affected regions. That is why people who had suffered from Naxalism also stood firmly with the government and the security forces. Even here today, there are citizens present who contributed greatly to this major victory. I express my gratitude to all of them as well.
Friends,
When we work with the spirit of Nation First, the country's peace and security are ensured, the nation reaches new heights of development, and the participation of every poor and deprived citizen in development also increases. Therefore, over the past twelve years, the country has not only won the fight against Naxalism and separatism, but it has also won a major battle against poverty.
Friends,
Just before Diwali this year, a piece of news emerged that is being discussed across the country and around the world. A few days ago, the World Bank stated in its report that in India, over the past twelve years, fifty crore people, fifty crore people, have risen out of extreme poverty. What decades of slogans about removing poverty could not achieve, the country accomplished in just twelve years. Just imagine how great an achievement this is. Think about how it became possible.
Friends,
During Diwali, we create rangoli designs. At first, only a few lines are drawn, and the initial patterns appear small and separate. But as one small part after another comes together, a beautiful and complete picture emerges. Over the past twelve years, something similar has happened in India. We created a rangoli of welfare schemes that continuously empowered the poor. Through the Jan Dhan Yojana, crores of people became connected to the banking system. Through the PM Awas Yojana, crores of families received permanent homes. Under the Mudra Yojana, we provided loans without collateral. Through the SVANidhi Scheme, street vendors also received support and opportunities to expand their businesses. Under Ayushman Bharat, we provided free healthcare to the poor. Crores of families received free food grains every month. Policies were created for children's education. In other words, we ensured free medicine, free education, and free kitchen support for every poor family. Not only that, schemes such as the Swachh Bharat Mission and Har Ghar Jal removed many basic concerns of daily life. As a result, crores of people have come out of poverty today. Families to whom poverty was once passed on as an inheritance are now inheriting the foundation of a better future. Families whose entire lives were spent in anxiety now have the confidence that comes from trust in the government and a renewed sense of self-belief.
Friends,
A major foundation of this victory against poverty is also linked to the country's fight against Naxalism and separatism. The people of Bastar and all of you know that wherever Naxalites held influence, their first agenda was to stop development and harm the lives of ordinary people. Schools for children were not allowed to function and were often set on fire. Hospitals for the sick were not allowed to be built, and doctors were prevented from entering. Facilities such as medical stores, which help save lives, were not permitted. These Naxalites even prevented children from receiving polio vaccinations. They did not allow mobile towers to be installed. You have seen for years how railway tracks were blown up with bombs and how industries and businesses were prevented from functioning. And the result was that lakhs of poor and innocent citizens, my brothers and sisters, and my young brothers and sisters, remained deprived of opportunities. Their lives never escaped the cycle of poverty. Therefore, when we began the fight against Naxalism, we simultaneously launched special campaigns for the development of Naxal-affected regions. We built more than 15,000 kilometres of roads in areas affected by Left-wing extremism, with complete security arrangements. More than 9,500 mobile towers were installed in these regions. Around 175 Eklavya schools were opened for the education of tribal children. Nearly 50 Industrial Training Institutes were established to connect youth with employment opportunities. Around 50 Skill Development Centres were created. Thousands of post offices, bank branches, and ATMs were opened. The PM Janman Yojana was launched for the development of the most backward tribal regions. Through this, facilities such as water, electricity, and roads reached thousands of remote villages for the first time. Not only this, surrendered Naxalites were also given an opportunity. Special schemes were created for their rehabilitation.
Friends,
This campaign of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas” has given the country's fight against poverty new energy and new confidence. That is why, on one hand, 50 crore people have come out of extreme poverty, and on the other hand, Naxalite violence has also come to an end in the country. Just look at Bastar itself. Today, the Bastar Olympics is being held in Bastar. Children are no longer picking up guns; they are trying their hands at sports.
Friends,
Amid these achievements, we must remember one more thing. The Naxalites have been eliminated, but the danger has not completely disappeared. Armed Naxalites have vanished from the forests, but intellectual Naxalites have captured many organisations. Even today, they are provoking people against the Constitution and democracy of the country. These intellectual Naxalites have also infiltrated several political parties and various organisations. We must identify them, defeat them, and secure the nation.
Friends,
Today's achievements inspire us, but they are not a pause. I say again, they are not a pause. These victories, these successes, are platforms for a new flight. This flight will carry the dreams of the nation, dreams that our generations have cherished for centuries. These will be the dreams of those freedom fighters who made countless sacrifices for independence. These will be the dreams of those brave soldiers who laid down their lives for Mother India on the nation's borders. These will be the dreams of those courageous personnel who sacrificed their lives in the fight against Naxalism and terrorism. Every day, you live by this spirit: "May your glory remain eternal, Mother. May your glory remain eternal, Mother. Whether we live for a few more days or not, May your glory remain eternal, Mother." Now is the time for this spirit of yours to transform into a new confidence. Now is the time to live for the nation and to take the nation to new heights.
Friends,
Whatever resolve our nation takes, it also possesses the capability to fulfil it. We had promised that we would remove Article 370 from Kashmir, and we fulfilled that promise. We had promised that we would build toilets in every household, and we fulfilled that promise. We had promised to expand the scope of vaccination, and we fulfilled that promise. Therefore, when we speak today about eliminating poverty, when we speak about a drug-free India, a narcotics-free India, when we speak about a Developed India, when we speak about a Self-Reliant India, these goals too will certainly be achieved. We must witness these dreams becoming reality before our very eyes. I have faith in you. I have faith in the youth power of my country. I have faith in the people of my nation. The country will certainly reach these goals. Your sacrifice and hard work will become the strong foundation of the grand edifice of a Developed India. With this faith, I once again extend my heartfelt greetings to all of you on the occasion of Diwali. Thank you all very much.
Bharat Mata Ki Jai.
Bharat Mata Ki Jai.
Bharat Mata Ki Jai.
Vande Mataram!
Vande Mataram!
Vande Mataram!
Vande Mataram!
Vande Mataram!
Vande Mataram!
Vande Mataram!
Thank you very much.
DISCLAIMER: This is the approximate translation of the Prime Minister’s address. Original address was delivered in Hindi.

title: 31,000 Devotees Seek Blessings of the Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha at Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh
subtitle: Seven-Day Exposition at Tawang Monastery Concludes on November 7; Sacred Relics to Be Enshrined at Bomdila from November 8
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 NOV 2026 11:44AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Sacred exposition of the Holy Relics of  Shakyamuni Buddha organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh and the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), New Delhi, concluded its Tawang leg today, 7 November 2026, after witnessing an overwhelming response from devotees and visitors. A total of 31,000 devotees and visitors visited Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) to have darshan of the sacred relics during the seven-day exposition.
The Sacred Relics arrived in Tawang on 31 October 2026 from the National Museum, New Delhi, with due protocol and ceremonial arrangements. The Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, Shri Pema Khandu, ceremonially received the sacred relics in the presence of the Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat.
The sacred exposition provided an opportunity for Buddhist monks, senior citizens and the general public to pay their respects, offer prayers and seek blessings in the presence of the sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha. Throughout the seven days, Tawang Monastery witnessed an outpouring of devotion, with devotees arriving from all blocks of Tawang district and neighbouring areas. The large turnout reflected the deep spiritual and cultural significance of the sacred relics among the people of the region.
As part of the exposition, the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh Shri Pema Khandu inaugurated two special exhibitions at Tawang Monastery. The exhibition ‘Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery’, organised by the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), showcased the historical discovery of the Piprahwa relics in 1898. The second exhibition, ‘Crossroads of Dhamma: Classical Legacies, Living Art, and Anthropological Perspectives’, curated by the National Museum, New Delhi, offered visitors an opportunity to explore the historical, artistic and cultural legacy of Buddhism and its enduring influence.
On 2 November 2026, the International Buddhist Confederation organised an international conference titled ‘Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond’ at the Kalawangpo Convention Centre, Tawang. The conference brought together Buddhist scholars, religious leaders and representatives from India and several other countries to deliberate on the dissemination and preservation of Buddhist teachings and heritage in the Himalayan region and beyond.
Following the conclusion of the sacred exposition at Tawang on 7 November, the Sacred Relics will continue their journey to  Bomdila as the next destination of exposition. On 8 November 2026, the Sacred Relics will be transported to Bomdila by the Indian Air Force. After a brief halt at Upper Gompa, the relics will be enshrined at TGL Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdila, where they will remain open for public darshan from 8 to 13 November 2026.
Thereafter, the Sacred Relics will move to the Golden Pagoda, Namsai, where the Sacred Relics will be available for public darshan from 14 to 20 November 2026, before returning to the National Museum, New Delhi, on 21 November 2026.
The exposition reflects the Government of India's continued commitment to preserving and promoting India's rich Buddhist heritage and strengthening the country's cultural and spiritual connections with Buddhist communities across the world.

title: Raksha Mantri celebrates Deepawali with troops in forward areas of Sikkim
subtitle:
Commends the courage, professionalism & dedication of soldiers guarding the borders in challenging high-altitude conditions

Shri Rajnath Singh honours fallen heroes at Sherathang War Memorial; pays respects at Baba Harbhajan Singh Memorial
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 NOV 2026 3:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh celebrated Deepawali with the soldiers of the Trishakti Corps (33 Corps) deployed in the forward areas of Sikkim, on November 8, 2026. He was accompanied by the Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth; General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Eastern Command Lt Gen VMB Krishnan; General Officer Commanding, 33 Corps Lt Gen Man Raj Singh Mann, and other senior officers of the Indian Army.
Interacting with the soldiers at Sherathang, Shri Rajnath Singh described them as the brightest lights of Diwali, stating that their dedication and vigilance at the borders provide the entire nation with a sense of security. “Like a lamp which dispels darkness without seeking attention, soldiers perform their duties silently, ensuring that citizens can celebrate festivals with peace and security,” he said.
Raksha Mantri commended the soldiers for their professionalism, high morale and steadfast commitment to safeguarding the Nation's borders in challenging high-altitude conditions, urging them to continue protecting the motherland with the same enthusiasm and dedication. He acknowledged the sacrifices of soldiers who serve far away from their families, placing duty to the Nation above self and personal celebrations.
Underlining the importance of discipline and courage, Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that no matter how advanced technology may become, it is of little use if a soldier lacks these qualities. He underlined that the conduct, uniform, language and restraint of the personnel shape the image of the military among local communities. He urged the soldiers to continue strengthening the bond of trust & goodwill shared by the Indian Army and the local population in Sherathang & surrounding areas.
Raksha Mantri also paid homage at the Sherathang War Memorial to the soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice in the service of the Nation. He also visited Baba Harbhajan Singh Memorial, paying his respects to the revered soldier whose legacy continues to hold a special place in the military-civil traditions of the region.
Highlighting the significance of the Sherathang War Memorial, Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that such monuments do more than commemorate past events and sacrifices; they shape collective memory and awaken national consciousness & pride. He stated that the soldiers honoured at the Memorial belonged to different parts of the country, including Nagaland, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan and Assam. He added that these bravehearts laid down their lives to protect the people, irrespective of their region, language or community. This spirit of unity and selfless service, he said, is the very soul and ethos of India, where every citizen considers fellow Indians as members of one family.
Raksha Mantri emphasised that the Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, established the National War Memorial in New Delhi to honour the gallant soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice in the service of the nation. “Approximately 26,000 names of the fallen heroes have been inscribed in golden letters at the National War Memorial to honour their unmatched valour and sacrifice. Seeing the name of a fallen soldier at the memorial evokes a deep sense of pride among their families, relatives and people from their native villages and regions. These memorials serve as sources of inspiration for the present and future generations.

title: Celebrate an Eco-Friendly Green Diwali for Cleaner Air: WWF-India EIACP appeals to citizens of Delhi-NCR to take the Green Diwali Pledge
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 NOV 2026 2:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
WWF-India's EIACP Programme Centre – Resource Partner (PC-RP), supported by the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC), Government of India, has appealed to the people of Delhi-NCR to celebrate a cracker-free Green Diwali this year and help keep the air clean. The appeal is part of the nationwide Green Diwali Campaign 2026, running from 20th October to 8th November 2026 under Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment), with a special focus on the 130 cities covered under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) across 24 States and Union Territories.
As per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Delhi's air quality is in the 'Very Poor' category, and as per the Air Quality Early Warning System forecasts it may reach the 'Severe' category during the festive days. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) is implementing measures under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across the region to prevent further deterioration of air quality. Citizens have been urged to support these efforts and follow the measures in force.
WWF EIACP has invited every citizen to take a Green Diwali Pledge to
perform their part for clean air, good health and a pollution-free environment. It has also laid out simple steps towards a Green Diwali, as below:
Choose Eco-Friendly Diyas and Candles:
Use traditional earthen diyas and eco-friendly candles, and avoid excessive energy consumption.
Go Sustainable with Gifts:
Choose locally made, eco-friendly gifts with minimal packaging.
Say No to Firecrackers:
Avoid firecrackers to help reduce air and noise pollution and protect public health.
Decorate Naturally:
Make rangolis using natural materials such as flower petals, rice flour and turmeric, and try DIY decorations using upcycled materials.
Minimise Waste:
Avoid single-use plastics, reuse decorations, and segregate waste for recycling.
Organise Community Events:
Host plantation drives, neighbourhood clean-up activities and environmental awareness walks to encourage collective action.
Donate for a Good Cause:
Donate old clothes and unused, usable household items to people in need, promoting reuse and reducing waste.
Adopt Greener Mobility:
Walk, cycle or use public or shared transport for festive travel whenever practical.
Check Your Air:
Follow the daily Air Quality Index (AQI) on the Central Pollution Control Board’s SAMEER app and limit outdoor exposure on poor air days.
Citizens have also been encouraged to take
WWF-India's Carbon Footprint Survey (
https://wwfindiawebgis.in/Carbon_Footprint/Carbon_Footprint.html
)
to understand their environmental footprint and adopt more sustainable habits. Further, participating institutions and groups have been invited to share their activities through the
online form -
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/15hDbjbqZzeo68kNjAxeHQA_SMIQ7lUlPdvCIi-gvwdY/viewform
.
Each submission should include the name and location of the institution or organisation, the activity details and date, the number of participants who took the pledge, geo-tagged photographs and a brief report. Selected entries may be featured on EIACP websites and social media platforms.

title: Shram Samvad: District Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes held in Dewas, Madhya Pradesh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                08 NOV 2026 9:11AM by PIB Delhi
content:
A District Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme, “Shram Samvad”, on Labour Codes, Labour Welfare and Social Protection, was jointly organized by Ministry of Labour & Employment (MoLE), Government of India (GoI) and Labour Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh in collaboration with Association of Industries Madhya Pradesh and M/s Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd at Dewas, Madhya Pradesh on 5th November, 2026.
The programme aimed at enhancing awareness among employers, HR, Legal and Finance professionals regarding the Labour Codes and rules made thereunder. It also focused on strengthening awareness and institutional capacity on labour reforms, welfare and social protection, promoting Centre-State coordination and stakeholder engagement.
Shri S.R. Datta, Director, MoLE
presided over the programme and participants included senior officials from MoLE, Labour Department, GoMP, Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) , Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) [CLC(C)], Directorate General Labour Welfare (DGLW) along with more than 100 participants from employers, industry representatives, legal, HR and finance professionals.
The programme featured a series of technical sessions designed to provide participants with practical insights into the Labour Codes, employer obligations, and key social security initiatives of the GoI.
Shri S.R. Datta, Director, MoLE
presented the keynote address highlighting the key features of the Labour Codes. Various sessions were conducted by officials from MoLE, focusing on the key compliance requirements for employers under each of the four Labour Codes and Central Rules notified under the Labour Codes. The sessions provided practical guidance on statutory obligations and compliance responsibilities, enabling participants to better understand the operational aspects of the new labour codes.
Representatives from EPFO and DGLW also led sessions on Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme, respectively.
To facilitate the employers and compliance professionals in effective implementation of the Labour Codes and Rules, ‘Handbook of Compliance for Employers’ and ‘Compilation of Frequently Asked Questions’
developed by MoLE were also shared with the participants.
An engaging Question and Answer session was also held, enabling participants to address their queries and gain greater clarity on the Labour Codes, compliance requirements, and social security provisions. By bringing together Central Government and State Government authorities and industry representatives, the event contributed to enhanced awareness, improved understanding, and stronger stakeholder engagement, thereby supporting the effective adoption and implementation of the New Labour Codes.
